summary: Join our Sustainable Land Use and Biodiversity Conservation Training Course to learn effective strategies for protecting ecosystems and promoting sustainability
lede: Sustainable landscape planning balances productive land use with habitat connectivity and ecological integrity. For land-use planners, environmental officers, conservation project managers, and related professionals, this course supports evidence-based decisions amid data gaps and competing land claims, with practice in biodiversity baselines, GIS-based sensitivity mapping, spatial prioritization, mitigation sequencing, and monitoring plans that connect field actions to ecological outcomes.
audienceIntro: This course is intended for professionals who already work with land, environment, conservation, or sustainability decisions and need a more structured way to link evidence to action.
prerequisites: Participants should have working knowledge of land management, environmental planning, conservation projects, or sustainability reporting. Prior exposure to GIS, biodiversity assessments, or environmental impact processes is helpful but not mandatory. No coding is required for completion, although familiarity with spreadsheets and map-based datasets will help you complete the exercises more quickly. Advanced concepts such as spatial prioritization and monitoring dashboards are taught at an operational application level rather than technical engineering depth.
